title: IPFS MCP confirmation protocol
description: Messages of the confirmation gate (ADR-0003, docs/mcp/0003-confirmation-and-auth.md). Tools of class write or destructive have no side effect until a human approves. Mechanism 1: clients that advertised elicitation get an MCP elicitation request, carried in an SEP-2322 multi round trip (InputRequiredResult, then InputRetry); the server never calls ServerSession.Elicit, which go-sdk v1.8.0 refuses on protocol 2026-07-28. The round trip's requestState is a server-signed binding handle, not consent: only the user's answer in inputResponses approves (RequestStateClaims, RequestStateAcceptance). Mechanism 2: every other session or principal gets a pending confirmation in the broker, resolved only by a human-presence resolver (paired IPFS Desktop window, macOS LocalAuthentication, Linux polkit, an AG-UI interrupt answered by a user gesture for the ui principal, or the headless --confirm=cli opt-in). Mechanism 3: with no resolver the call is refused (confirmation_unavailable). The two-step confirm token is a binding handle, not consent: it is accepted only after its pending confirmation was approved by mechanism 1 or 2, it is never issued to or accepted from principals of kind a2a or uar, and it guarantees the executed call is exactly the confirmed call (same session, principal, tool and canonical arguments; single use).

Summary.description: What the user is asked to approve. text is rendered from the catalog confirmationSummary template and names the CID, path or name affected.

ElicitationRequest.description: MCP elicitation/create request for a client that advertised the elicitation capability. On the wire it is the value of inputRequests.confirm in an InputRequiredResult (SEP-2322); the SDK delivers it to the client's user.

_meta.description: Supported SDK _meta extension point. Preserve unrelated protocol metadata; validate this namespace only.

ElicitationResult.description: Client answer, the value of inputResponses.confirm in an InputRetry. Only action accept with content.confirm true approves; decline, cancel, accept without confirm true, or a missing answer abort with no side effect.

_meta.description: Supported SDK _meta extension point. Preserve unrelated protocol metadata; validate this namespace only.

ConfirmationRequired.description: Carried in ToolError.error.confirmation. code confirmation_required: a new pending confirmation was created; code confirmation_pending: a token or retry arrived while it is still pending. Repeating the call never approves it; only a resolver in resolvers does.

state.description: Approved confirmations never appear here: an approved call runs.

resolvers.description: Human-presence resolvers that may approve this confirmation, in order of preference. Never contains token.

confirm_token.description: Binding handle for sessions of kind human-mcp that cannot elicit: after a resolver approves, repeat the same call with this token to run it exactly once. Rejected (confirmation_pending, confirmation_declined or confirmation_expired) unless the confirmation is approved. Never present for principals of kind a2a or uar.

requires_native_prompt.description: Same meaning as PendingConfirmation.requires_native_prompt: true for destructive calls from the ui and a2a principals (ADR-0003 Round 7 amendment). Only a presence resolver (macos-localauth or linux-polkit) decides; desktop never counts, even with Touch ID in its window (ADR-0003, amendment of 2026-10-12; it still resolves write-class confirmations when the operator enables it), and cli and agui-interrupt never do, and with no presence resolver available the call is refused with confirmation_unavailable. An in-chat surface must not offer an approve control and may only offer deny. Absent means false.

ConfirmTokenClaims.description: Fields bound by the token's HMAC-SHA256 (per-process random key). The encoded token is opaque to clients; these fields are fixed so the binding is reviewable and testable. args_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of the arguments without confirm_token. The server accepts the token only when the pending confirmation cid is in state approved, then moves it to executed. executed records approval consumption before invocation; actual success is additive ExecutionRecord/SuccessfulReceipt data. This amendment does not change v1 claims, signing, args_sha256 or acceptance.

sid.description: MCP session ID (stdio: a per-process random ID).

exp.description: Expiry, Unix seconds. Expiry is denial.

use.description: Domain separation from RequestStateClaims, which the server signs with the same key. Optional in claims version 1 for compatibility; a server that signs request states with the confirm-token key must set it and must reject a token whose use is not confirm_token.

Resolver.description: Authorized resolver mechanisms. They are distinct from descriptive ResolvingSurface attribution. The confirm token, effect digest and observation access are deliberately not resolvers. Only macos-localauth/linux-polkit provide the native-presence factor; desktop never does.

PendingConfirmation.description: Broker record for out-of-band resolution. Transitions: pending to approved, denied or expired; approved to executed exactly once. Additive display/outcome fields do not change those transitions. executed is a single-use consumption claim before the handler runs, never a success receipt. principal remains the configured display principal, never its raw identity BindingKey; use DecisionObservation for identity-scoped read projections.

principal.description: Legacy configured principal display name. Never serialize the internal identity BindingKey or OIDC subject here.

resolver.description: Legacy resolver mechanism; when resolved_by is present they must agree. Neither identifies the browser surface.

requires_native_prompt.description: True for destructive calls from the ui and a2a principals: neither a chat answer nor an A2A message nor cli approves; only a presence resolver (macos-localauth or linux-polkit) does; desktop never counts.

Outcome.description: Result reported when a confirmation ends without execution.

TokenAcceptance.description: Decision table for a presented token (all other checks passing: signature, single use, session, principal, tool, arguments, expiry).

RequestState.description: Opaque, server-signed handle for one elicitation round trip: base64url claims (RequestStateClaims) followed by an HMAC-SHA256 under the per-process key. Clients echo it unchanged and never interpret it. It is not consent and never approves a call by itself.

InputRequiredResult.description: First tool result for a write or destructive call from a session that advertised elicitation (SEP-2322 multi round trip, go-sdk resultType input_required). The call has no side effect. The server opens a pending confirmation for mechanism elicitation and asks the user through inputRequests.confirm. The SDK obtains the answer (client side from protocol 2026-07-28, server side before) and retries the call as an InputRetry.

InputRetry.description: Params of the retried tools/call. name and arguments must be the first call's (the canonical arguments hash is rechecked); arguments never carry confirm_token on this path. requestState is echoed from the InputRequiredResult.

_meta.description: Supported SDK _meta extension point. Preserve unrelated protocol metadata; validate this namespace only.

RequestStateClaims.description: Fields bound by the request state's HMAC. Same binding as ConfirmTokenClaims (session, principal, tool, canonical arguments, expiry, single-use nonce) plus use, which keeps the two handles apart: a confirm token is never accepted as a request state, and a request state is never accepted as a confirm token. cid names a confirmation opened by mechanism elicitation; a request state for a confirmation opened for external resolution is invalid.

exp.description: Equals the confirmation's expires_at. Expiry is denial.

RequestStateAcceptance.description: Decision table for an InputRetry. state_check is evaluated first: valid means the HMAC verifies, use is request_state, session, principal, tool and arguments match, the session advertised elicitation at initialize, the confirmation exists and was opened by mechanism elicitation, and the request state has not expired. Only then does the user's answer count, and only while the confirmation is pending. The opposite of TokenAcceptance, which requires approved: a request state never carries an approval, it only lets the answer in inputResponses resolve the confirmation it names.

state_check.description: tampered: HMAC or encoding fails. wrong_use: a confirm token presented as a request state. other_call: session, principal, tool or arguments differ. not_eliciting: the session did not advertise elicitation, or the confirmation was opened for external resolution. unknown: no such confirmation. expired: exp passed.

answer.description: accept_confirmed is action accept with content.confirm true; every other value denies.

EffectDigest.description: Server-computed SHA-256 of canonicalJSON({arguments: validated token-free arguments actually supplied, tool: canonical tool name}). Retain existing argsDigest canonicalization and token bytes. Omitted defaults are not inserted; explicit defaults remain explicit. Exclude only top-level confirm_token from arguments; transport/session/resolver/surface metadata is outside this envelope. A digest is an effect binding, never consent.

Destination.description: Safe configured destination display label from known operation semantics, never arbitrary model text, credentialed URL or secret. Omit when unknown. It does not select an endpoint or alter the call.

ResolvingSurface.description: Descriptive attribution only; instance is a bounded opaque per-surface identifier, not a principal or credential. Distinguishes two chat panes. Browser attribution never selects an authorized resolver. Trusted native/MCP adapters stamp their own kind.

DecisionId.description: Opaque read-side identifier, not a confirmation token or authorization handle. UAR synthetic IDs remain separate from broker confirmations.

DecisionApprovalState.description: Legacy approval lifecycle. executed means approval was consumed exactly once before invocation, not that the operation succeeded. Missing execution metadata never upgrades it to Done.

DecisionPresentation.description: Derived client presentation, not broker state or authorization. Successful receipt takes precedence over surface attribution; known failure maps to failed_after_approval, ambiguity to uncertain. Defined by confirmation/README.md; eleven values, one generated shared model.

SafeExecutionError.description: Bounded public error detail. No raw RPC/backend bodies, stack traces, credentials, content bytes or sensitive arguments. Known failure does not establish zero effects.

ReceiptReference.description: Actual confirmed result identifier, never guessed from input or arbitrary tool prose. No fetched content, secret key bytes, credentialed URL or backend response body.

SuccessfulReceipt.description: Success evidence for one immutable decision/tool/digest, created only from the actual handler result or a correlated validated backend operation report. An accepted background job proves job_accepted only. Empty result_refs is honest for success without returned identifiers. A text TOOL_CALL_RESULT or UAR RUN_FINISHED success is insufficient. Result delivery/serialization failure after recorded success does not undo it.

ExecutionRecord.description: At most one invocation owns this record. not_started -> running -> succeeded | failed | unknown. A later reliable correlated report may refine unknown; it never authorizes another invocation. Only succeeded has a SuccessfulReceipt. Known failure means a definite unsuccessful operation result, not no partial effects; ambiguous partial effects/transport loss stay unknown. Timestamps and receipt bindings must agree semantically. When both timestamps exist, started_at <= completed_at; equality is valid at the observed clock resolution. Clamp a backwards wall-clock completion to started_at; never invent a +1ns interval. Receipt completion equals record completion.

oneOf.description: Actual operation lifecycle, separate from the one-time approval claim.

Dispatch/outcome evidence is insufficient; no retry or zero-effect claim.

DecisionAuthority.description: Safe configured display identity. Omit unknown name. Never expose raw OIDC subject, BindingKey, session grant or credentials. Observation is filtered privately by the full identity binding across its sessions.

DecisionEgress.description: Actual operation/egress-policy facts only. none requires evidence that the operation sends no content to a third-party service; absence does not imply none. This display is not an egress acknowledgement.

DecisionContinuation.description: Capability-scoped locator for the current identity's exact open chat interruption. Uses the existing authenticated resume path; not a generic confirmation resolver. No bearer, confirm token, requestState, backend grant or raw args. Server rechecks owner/interrupt/expiry/digest/resolver; this locator conveys no authority by itself.

DecisionActions.description: Current authenticated capability hints, rechecked at resolution. Only owned open chat interruptions may carry continuation; other records name the known authorized surface or omit it honestly. Native-required observations never enable approve. Read/item/feed access cannot create resolver rights.

DecisionSummary.description: Bounded prepared-operation display from catalog/known semantics; targets supply scope. No sensitive raw arguments, content bytes or unsanitized backend/model prose. Large target sets use a bounded truthful summary rather than silently implying completeness.

DecisionObservation.description: Safe identity-scoped read-side projection for the later list/item/feed contract. Never include principal binding keys, other identities' native requests, raw arguments, tokens/requestState or credentials. kubo/node_confirmation denotes a broker decision; uar/backend_approval denotes UAR-only approval, not consent for this node. Summary carries tool/class/object/targets; destination names the effect target, actions.authorized_surface names where it may be answered. Absent facts remain unreported.

ReviewedEffect.description: Optional transport-level echo of exactly the digest the person reviewed. Never a tool argument or consent. Upgraded adapters compare it before resolving; omission retains all legacy identity, immutable tool/argument, expiry, mechanism and single-use checks. An inconsistent supplied value fails with confirmation_digest_mismatch and never claims approval.

ReviewDisplayMetadata.description: Value of ElicitParams._meta['ipfs-mcp']; safe prepared digest and optional destination, never consent. Omit unknown destination rather than null.

ReviewResponseMetadata.description: Value of ElicitResult._meta['ipfs-mcp'] or tools/call params._meta['ipfs-mcp']. Optional echo only; if both supplied, require valid identical values after existing binding checks. No new resolver rights.

NativeResolveRequest.description: Body of the existing authenticated POST /v1/resolve on private native confirmation Unix socket. Optional signed-body echo; no new public decisions resolver or pairing/protocol version. Existing native factor/resolver/expiry/sender checks remain.

ToolOutcomeMetadata.description: Optional value of CallToolResult._meta['ipfs-mcp'] for the authorized current node operation after its winning claim. A detached actual execution snapshot, not consent or another result payload. Receipt is only execution.receipt. No BindingKey, raw arguments/results, tokens, prompt or authority handles. Preserve all legacy response fields and other metadata.

confirmation_id.description: The actual node broker ID for this current call. No synthetic UAR approval ID.

ToolOutcomeResultMeta.description: The optional standard CallToolResult._meta map. Other existing metadata such as ai.ipfs/tool and ai.ipfs/untrusted-content stays intact. No required ipfs-mcp key: legacy tool results remain valid.

ActivityId.description: Opaque server-assigned correlation ID for a newly accepted user activity, stable across its authorized resumes. Not a client-selected run/thread ID, ownership key, authorization handle, content identifier or durable history promise. Never encode a BindingKey, principal, subject, token or sensitive arguments.
